title: Pranamami Prabhupad Padam
subtitle: Śrī Chaitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha
description: Pranamami Prabhupad Padam — a themed treasury of teachings gathered by the Śrī Chaitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha.

articles.title: On the Disappearance Day of Srila Prabhupad
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: In the initial part of harikatha, Srila Gurudev narrates about how Srila Param Gurudev acquired the appearance place of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur at Puri-dham. Then he narrates how Lord Jagannath stayed three days in front of Srila Bhaktivinod Thakur’s house at Puri when Srila Saraswati Thakur was of six months. He also narrated about how Srila Saraswati Thakur approached Srila Gaurkishor Das Babaji repeatedly for his shelter.

blocks.text: The functions which remind us about Guru, Vaishnav and Bhagavan destroys all our in-auspiciousness and fulfills our spiritual desires. As a proof, you can see that by the mercy of Narada Risi, Vedavyas Muni could realize the pastimes of the Supreme Lord and wrote Srimad Bhagavatam. He is the father as well as the spiritual master of Sukadeva Goswami. He made him to listen to Srimad Bhagavatam at the bank of Saraswati River in Badrikashram. Vedavyas Muni was the speaker and Sukadeva Goswami was the listener. Though, Sukadeva Goswami was fully established in Brahman realization by his birth, by hearing the pastimes of Supreme Lord, he became fully absorbed in the Divine love of Sri Krishna. And after that he did not give any value to the bliss of Brahman realization for which the great gyanis and Munis perform severe penances for thousands and thousands years but still they do not get it. Bliss obtained in Brahman realization is equivalent to the water retained in the foot impression of a cow. And the Divine Love of Krishna is equivalent to the water of a fathomless ocean. Krishna is the madhuryamaya-vigrah—the embodiment of highest sweet mellow. He is avatari—the cause of all other avataras. After describing all the avataras, Rama, Nrisimha etc. in Srimad Bhagavatam, Vedavyasa Muni wrote,

“All of the above-mentioned avataras are either plenary portions or portions of the plenary portions of the Lord, but Lord Sri Krishna is the original Supreme Lord. All of them appear on planets whenever there is a disturbance created by the atheists. The Lord descends to protect the theists.”

So, Krishna is svayam bhagavan—the original Supreme Person. Chatuhsan—Sanak, Sanatan, Sanandan and Sanat, the four Kumaras, were completely absorbed in the bliss of Brahman realization. When they attained the aroma of Tulsi offered to lotus feet of Narayan, they at once became attracted towards the lotus feet of the Lord and they immediately became devotees. They abandoned their long-cherished impersonalism straight away. The madhurmaya-vigrah of the Supreme Lord, towards whom even Narayan also gets attracted is, Nandanandan Sri Krishna. Krishna gave instructions making Uddhava the medium in eleventh Canto of Srimad Bhagavatam. He says to Uddhava, “In Brahman realization, one cannot get even an iota of bliss in comparison with the transcendental bliss that the Gopis have because of their loving devotion for Sri Krishna. They do not know the ontological aspects of Mine. They do not know Me as the Supreme Lord.”

Srila Prabhupad appeared in Jagannath Dham, Purushottam Dham. That place is situated not far from the Jagannath Temple on the Grand Road in Puri and was constantly reverberating with the sound of Harinam. Six months after the appearance of the child, it was time for the Rathayatra festival. That year, by Lord Jagannath’s desire, His chariot stopped in front of Sri Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s house and simply would not move forward. Under Bhaktivinoda Thakura’s direction, a sankirtan festival was held in front of the Deity for the entire three-day and night. That place is known as Narayan Chhata. ‘Chhatta’ in Oriya language is umbrella. Now a big temple is established at that place. Our Guruji has established that temple because many God brothers of our Gurudev came to him and requested, “You have established so many Maths at various places in India but in Puri, the appearance place of our Gurudev (Prabhupad) has been occupied by many tenants from long time. We have to pay our obeisances from outside, sometimes even that is not possible. We do not see anyone else other than you who can rescue that place.”

My body is from Bengal, you do not know my language properly and I do not know your language properly so it is little difficult to explain. I have Bengali accent so you have to hear very attentively. If you do not pay proper attention then you will not be able to understand. So there were so many tenants, who occupied that place since more than forty years. It was very difficult to draw them out from that place. Who would go there to have the place vacated? Even the organization such as ISKCON ran away from there. No one was keen to procure the place. Our Guruji went to Srila Tirtha Maharaj, who was the President of Chaitanya Math that time, even he did not show any interest in procuring that place. Then many of the God-brothers of Guruji came to him and they requested him to take that task in his hand. Our Guruji had a special characteristic, whatever he speaks, he would do that. Guruji thought, “All the Vaishanava are giving me the order to rescue that place.” He was always in the mood of, gopī-bhartuḥ pada-kamalayor dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥs—identifying oneself only as the servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of Lord Sri Krishna, the maintainer of the gopis. So he took responsibility to vacate that place and to take custody of it. There were so many challenges involved in acquiring that place that it was almost impossible to make it happen. I requested Guruji, “No one is worried about acquiring that place. Your health is not good. So it will be good if you do not take such a hard work. There are no proper arrangements here for your stay. You have to stay in Dharmashala (lodge), there are so many ants here and you cannot get proper sleep in the night at such a place. What will be the benefit we would get by taking so much pain and doing so much hard work? Please you leave this task.”
Gurudev did not give any response to my words. Rather he told me to write an application. He said, “Tomorrow, I will meet the Chief Minister.”

Guruji’s nature was like that if he would take any task in his hand then he would surely complete it. He was thinking all Vaishanava had given him responsibility so he would fulfill their desire. He used to make the impossible possible. We were thinking that the place had so many controversies and so many court cases had been filed, so even if we would get that place, it would not be possible to get the possession of the place. But Guruji took the responsibility to procure that place and many big personalities like Rangnath Mishra, the chief justice of Supreme Court and Gangadhar Mahapatro came in his full support. Would such personalities come in support of any ordinary person like me? But they came behind our Guruji, being attracted by His exalted personality. He made the impossible task possible. When we try to serve Supreme Lord without any deceitfulness, nothing is impossible, our Gurudev is teaching us through his life. In the commentary of Gita, Vishvanath Chakravartypad gave an example, we should remember it.

There was a tiny sparrow, who laid her eggs on the shore of the ocean. She had strong attachment for her eggs. Once she was not there near her eggs. That time the water level in ocean rose up, as always happens with the tides in the oceans. The big ocean carried away the eggs on its wave. The sparrow became very upset when she returned back. She asked other birds about her eggs, they replied, “The ocean carried away so many valuable things, what is the value of your tiny eggs? You will get new eggs again.” She was not convinced by their opinion and approached the ocean. She paid obeisance and requested the ocean to return her eggs back. She said she has not committed any offense to him, why should he take her eggs? But the ocean did not respond to her request. She prayed many a times but the ocean did not even consider her appeal, so she became angry and decided to dry up the ocean. Is a tiny sparrow capable of drying up the ocean? But she jumped in to the water of the ocean and began to pick out a small drop of water in her small beak. Everyone laughed at her for her impossible determination. They advised her to stop her endeavors, as she would never be able to dry up the ocean and the whole cast of birds would be blasphemed for her foolish act. But she did not listen to any one and continued with her efforts. By divine arrangement, Narada Goswami was passing through that place and he saw the small sparrow’s act. He knew the language of birds, so he went to her and asked her, “What are you doing? Why you are doing so?” In reply she explained everything to him.

Narada Goswami advised her, “See! You would never be able to dry up the ocean by your endeavors. You are wasting your time. Leave it. Whatever happened, happened by the divine arrangement. You may get eggs again.”

But she fell down at the lotus feet of Narada Muni and told him, “I do not have any enmity towards the ocean, if he will return my eggs then I will stop. By drying up the ocean I will get my eggs back.”

Narada Muni is the personified form of mercy of the Supreme Lord. She fell at his lotus feet so she received his mercy. Narada Muni went to Vaikuntha to the Garuda. He told Garuda, “Even in your presence your community is getting blasphemed, I saw it.” Upon being asked by Garuda, Narada Muni described everything to him. He also told Garuda that whole world is laughing at the sparrow, which belongs to his bird community.
Garuda asked Narada Muni, “What should I do now?” Narada Muni replied, “You go there and do something so that that tiny bird will get her eggs back.”

Garuda immediately arrived and attacked the ocean with his huge wings. The personification form of the ocean came there and asked about the reason behind Garuda’s act. Garuda replied, “You have carried away the eggs of this small sparrow and you are not giving them back. You are insulting our bird community, you have to return the eggs.” The ocean was frightened at this and returned the eggs. That tiny sparrow did not have any capability but when someone continues his endeavors, sincerely, with firm faith then he will get help from above. Our Gurudev continued his endeavors to get that place so Lord Jagannath and his Gurudev, Srila Prabhupad came to his support and made the impossible task possible. We got the place and all the tenants went away and later a big temple was established there. When the tenants left that place, all the exalted Vaishnava Sanyasis were invited there. Srila Bon Maharaj and other Vaishanava came there and a big celebration was held in that old building. After that function, Gurudev left this material world and entered into eternal pastime of Supreme Lord. After the departure of Gurudev, we were thinking, how would we establish a temple at that place? How would that task be completed? But our Gurudev arranged everything!

One day, I was walking on a road in Puri. That time one unknown person got out from his car and came to me and gave me five hundred rupees. Keshava Prabhu and Krishnadas Babaji Maharaj were there with me and he gave three hundred rupees to each of them. We were surprised, how a person could give so much money to some unknown people while walking on the road? What was going on? It had never happened before. We thought Guruji was giving us a signal to go to that person for help. We did not have any courage to establish a big temple, we were worried. So our Gurudev guided us to go to that person for help. Gurudev made that person a medium. A huge Math was established there. Who did it? Our Gurudev did it. Though externally he was not present there but he only did everything. We did not do anything. We were worried and prayed to him, “We have this place but now what will happen? How will the temple be established?” And so our Gurudev guided us. It is a real incident. It is not a story. Because it is the appearance place of our Param Gurudev, people from all over the world come there.

Today is the disappearance day of our Param Gurudev. He enacted his disappearance pastime at Bagbazar Gaudiya Math, Kolkata. He was in Puri before, from there he went to Bagbazar Gaudiya Math. He stayed in this world for sixty three years. He appeared in this world in 1874 and left the world and entered in the predawn pastimes (Nishant-lila, the first yam pastime that we read during Kartik month daily) of the Supreme Lord at 5.30 a.m. on Friday 1st, January, 1937. According to the Western calendar after twelve midnight the new day starts.

It is written by Sri Vyasadeva Risi in the Padma-Purana, ‘hy utkale purusottamāt’, the message of pure devotion to Sri Krishna will be spread throughout the world from Jagannath Puri. And after the appearance of our Param Gurudev, Srila Saraswati Thakur, who descended accepting Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur and Srimati Bhagavati Devi as his parents, devotion to Sri Krishna was spread throughout the world. He was endowed with transcendental powers. He performed a sacrifice of chanting hundred crores of Holy Names which he completed in nine years. He observed Chaturmasya-vrata in Mayapur Dham. He did go-grass (eating like a cow without using his hands by serving the Prasadam on the floor) for these four months.
Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu appeared to distribute the highest Divine love to the conditioned souls of the world. He declared,
“In every town and village of the earth, the chanting of My name will be propagated.”

After the disappearance of Sri Krishna Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Svarupa Damodar, Ramananda Raya, the Six Goswamis, Srinivas Acharya, Narottam Das Thakur and Shyamananda Prabhu, a dark age descended on the world of Gaudiya Vaisnavism. Why did that happen? We should deeply think about that. Was there no scholar at that time? Was there no Bhagavatam that time? Or the books of six Goswamis, Chaitanya Charitamrita or Chaintanya Bhagavat? Everything was there, but no one could understand the doctrine of pure devotion. And because of that numerous pseudo-sects or apasampradayas cropped up. The Westerners translate apasampradaya to heretic-sects which does not clearly represent the word. The more appropriate translation is pseudo or false sects. Totaram Das Babaji Maharaj named thirteen such pseudo-sects and prohibited everyone from associating with them.

blocks.text: The pseudo-sect people claimed that they also preach the message of Mahaprabhu but they are practicing and spreading the opposite of His real teachings. In the name of religion they keep elicit connections with woman. Their character is not good. They do not have the scriptural knowledge. At the time of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, the whole of Bengal was influenced by His teachings but after He left to go back to the transcendental abode the pseudo sect people practiced and propagated His teachings inappropriately and the influence of Mahaprabhu’s teachings was diminished. No one could understand the real implication of those teachings. Preaching the message of pure devotion is not so easy. At first, one should judge his own character. No one will get benefited just by merely giving instructions to others. One must practice the teachings of pure devotion in his whole life. One’s whole life must be dedicated for the service of Sri Krishna. One should have unconditional surrender to the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord. There should not be any other motive. As long as misconception of the self is there, evil desires will automatically come. Who can stop them?
Mahadeva, who is the Guru of Vaishnava and the origin of Rudra-sampraday, which is one among the four Vaishnav-sampraday, told Parvatidevi,
“There are many so called guru to squeeze out the wealth of the disciples but a sadguru is very rare to be found who takes away all the miseries of the disciple.”

It is very rare to find a sadguru in this world. If you want quantity, you will not get quality. One person with a good character can do immense good to crores and crores of people. But crores and crores of characterless persons cannot do good to even a single person. Quality is important. The medicine invented by one scientist can benefit six hundred crores people of the world. If you want quantity, you have to sacrifice quality. Persons with good qualities are always less in number. Therefore Mahadeva explained as such.

Mahaprabhu knew that nobody had understood and in future nobody would understand the real implication of His teachings by reading them from books, as conditioned souls have the misconception of the self and different worldly motives. He then decided to send someone from His associates to rescue the fallen souls and Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur came to this world. Accepting him, Srila Saraswati Thakur appeared in this world. Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur wrote more than one hundred books in different languages and refuted all the anti-devotional ideologies. He restarted the World Vaishnava Association (Vishva Vaishnava Rajsabha) in Kolkata. Srila Saraswati Thakur used to go with him carrying Bhakti-rasamrit-sindhu. He was a young boy that time. There used to be a World Vaishnav Association (WVA) meeting every Sunday. At present Paramdveti Maharaj from Germany is carrying out special efforts to have these meetings. He requested me to be the vice-president and then the president of WVA. I will continue to follow the order of Vaishnava as long as I have the capability.

It was the desire of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur and Srila Saraswati Prabhupad to continue WVA meetings. Not only Gaudiya Vaishnavas, but Vaishnavas from Ramanuja-sampraday, Vishnuswami, Nimbaditya and many other Vaishnavas were part of WVA that time.

Our Bhaktisiddhant Saraswati Prabhupad refuted all the anti-devotional ideologies. The Brahmins of Nabadvip Dham started charging money for having darshan of the deity in temples. Srila Saraswati Thakur Prabhupad opposed their acts as Mahaprabhu distributed the highest Divine Love to everyone without considering any material qualification of caste, religion or anything. He distributed the love to everyone whoever came in contact with Him. So making His deity the medium to earn money is not at all appropriate. He also opposed the acts of persons who made reading Srimad Bhagavatam as their source of income. Because he refuted all these anti-devotional thoughts and actions, they all became enraged towards him and many of them tried to harm him in various ways. They even tried to kill him but they were completely unsuccessful. Prabhupad did not take any of their acts as an offense. But whoever came to harm or to try and kill Prabhupad were all drowned in the Ganges. Srila Prabhupad was aggrieved on listening to their fate. Others who also were opposing him became very scared of doing any harm to him.

Srila Saraswati Prabhupad expanded his energy by transmitting his powers to his disciples and preached the message of pure devotion throughout the world. He established sixty-four centers all over India. He established the assembly for spreading the glories of Nabadvip Dham (Nabadvip-dham-pracharini-sabha). He sent his disciples to London, Germany and many other places. Srila Swami Maharaj who preached the message of devotional service to the Supreme Lord in Western countries was ordered by Srila Saraswati Thakur Prabhupad to do so. I did not know this before. I had gone to have his darshan, as he is the God-brother of our Gurudev, at RadhaDamodar temple, Vrindavan where he was staying after his Sanyas. That time he showed me his ‘Back to Home, Back to Godhead’—monthly magazine. It was very indistinct printing, difficult to read. I requested him, “Our Gurudev is here in Sree Chaitanya Gaudiya Math. Will you not go our Math?” He replied, “Yes.” Next day he came and he entered into the room of our Gurudev and talked to Gurudev for more than half an hour, or more than that perhaps. I was outside. I do not know what topic they spoke upon, they are God-brothers. When he came out and was leaving, he called me at the gate. He said, “I have got the desire to go outside India to preach Chaitanya Mahaprabhu’s message, will you go with me?” That time I was the secretary of Sree Chaitanya Gaudiya Math and there were many incomplete services, in Chandigarh Math, in Puri Math, in Mayapur Math, all these were incomplete in terms of construction and I had the responsibility to complete. What could I do? I remained silent. He was disappointed. He could not get any help. He went to Western countries alone. Later, when I had gone to Western countries, I was taken to different places visited by Swami Maharaj by Vaikuntha Nath Das Prabhu. He was a professor and a disciple of Swami Maharaj. He came by Lord’s desire and helped me to go different places. While coming back from a function at Connecticut to New York, which is a two hour journey, he asked me, “May I listen to my Gurudev’s sermons on tape record?” I replied, “Yes, Yes. I shall be benefited by that.” There I heard Srila Swami Maharaj’s sermon delivered on the disappearance day of Srila Saraswati Prabhupad.

He says in that, “All my god-brothers were engaged in the service of Prabhupad but as I was a householder, I was endeavoring to earn money for the maintenance of my family. In that regard, I came to Mumbai from Kolkata. I was trying hard to earn money. That time I got the news that Srila Gurudev’s (Prabhupad’s) health is not good. He may leave this material world at any time. That time I wrote a letter to him saying I am your disciple, I am a fallen soul, everybody is engaged in your service but I do not have opportunity to serve you. You please instruct me on what service I shall do.”
In reply to his letter, Srila Prabhupad wrote, “You have good hold over English. You can preach the message of Divine love throughout the globe.”

“I got that letter of Srila Gurudev. I was thinking I have to carry out his order but I could not act upon it immediately and that time I got the message that Srila Gurudev has departed to his eternal abode.”

Last Narayan 4, 450 of the Chaitanya era, at the end of the Thursday night, Paush 16, 1343 of the Bengali calendar, on Friday morning, January 1, 1937, Srila Prabhupad, joined his eternal service in the pre-dawnpredawn pastimes (nisanta-lila) of Sri Radha-Govinda. That time, Swami Maharaj completely renounced worldly life and took Sanyas-ashram. He was always praying to Narottam Thakur and Bhaktivinoda Thakur through their kirtans for their grace so that he can fulfill the desire of his Gurudev, Srila Prabhupad.

Srila Saraswati Prabhupad met his Gurudev, Srila Gaura Kishor Das Babaji Maharaj in 1900. Babaji Maharaj used to come to Godrum-dvipa at the place of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur from Nabadvip. He used to sing the kirtan, ‘vṛndāvana-vilāsinī, rādhe, rādhe , kānu-mana-mohinī, rādhe, rādhe'. Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur ordered Srila Saraswati Thakur to take deeksha from Srila Gaura Kishor Das Babaji Maharaj. Srila Saraswati Prabhupad went to him and prayed to him to accept him as his disciple. But Babaji Maharaj refused to give him deeksha as he wanted to perform devotion in solitude without accepting any disciple. When someone accepts a disciple then he has to think about the ultimate welfare of the disciple. Srila Babaji Maharaj used to live beneath a broken boat with utmost renunciation.
Srila Prabhupad asked Gaura Kishor Das Babaji Maharaja several times to give him initiation. The first time he asked, Babaji Maharaja told him, “If Mahaprabhu tells me to, I will.”

The second time Babaji Maharaja told him that he had forgotten to ask Mahaprabhu. Srila Prabhupad did not give up and came a third time. Babaji Maharaja said, “Virtuousness, scholarship and other qualities are not the means to attain the Lord. They do not give you any right for initiation.”
Though he had been turned away by Gaura Kishor Das Babaji repeatedly, Srila Prabhupad did not abandon his resolution.

Srila Prabhupad showed his qualities of patience and determination as he continued to come before Babaji Maharaja. He humbly entreated him to give him initiation until finally his heart melted, and out of great affection mercifully he initiated Srila Prabhupad by sprinkling the dust of his lotus feet on his head. He said, “You are eligible to propagate the message of Mahaprabhu throughout the world.” He then gave him deeksha-mantra and transmitted all the powers to him. Then Prabhupad performed sacrifice of performing hundred crores of Holy Names. He accepted sanyas-ashram in 1918 and established Chaitanya Math. He thought, “I do not have wealth or people, how can I propagate the message of Mahaprabhu? But it is the order of my Gurudev so I have to follow it.”

He was not an ordinary person, he was very powerful. Many great scholars came to him to refute the doctrine of pure devotion but on having seen his effulgent personality they could not even talk to him let alone try to refute his thoughts. In 1911, there was some debate that took place between Brahmins and Vaishnava. That time Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur was exhibiting the pastimes of ill health. Viswambharnath Goswami, a great scholar and the grandfather of Atul Krishna Goswami of RadhaRaman temple, also took part in that discussion. Everybody was astonished to hear Srila Prabhupad speak at such a young age on the differences between Brahmins and Vaishnava. Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur was contemplating on who will propagate the doctrine of pure devotion after his departure. The grandfather of Atul Krishna Goswami, after listening to Srila Prabhupad in that assembly, went to Bhaktivinoda Thakur and very joyfully told him that his disciple Srila Saraswati Thakur Prabhupad is capable of propagating the pure devotional doctrine.

After the disappearance of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur and Gaura Kishor Das Babaji Maharaj, one night, however, Prabhupad had a svapna-samadhi (dream-like vision) in which he saw all the members of the Pancha Tattva, being led by Mahaprabhu in Sankirtan, dancing and approaching toward the birthplace at the Yoga Pith in Mayapur, from the eastern side of its Natya-mandira. They were followed by the Six Goswamis and by Vaishnava Sarvabhauma Jagannath Das Babaji, Bhaktivinoda Thakura, Gaura Kishor Das Babaji Maharaj and other guruvarga members of the disciplic succession, all appearing in effulgent, divine forms. They consoled Prabhupad, saying, “Why are you worrying? Get the task of preaching pure devotion underway. Preach Mahaprabhu’s message everywhere. Spread the service to Gaura-dhama (Mahaprabhu’s abode), Gaura-nama (His Name), and Gaura-kama (His desire or work). All of us are ready to support you at every turn. We will help you at every moment in your efforts to preach pure devotional service. Countless people, unlimited wealth and extraordinary scholarship are all waiting for you to call for them. Whenever you need anything at all, it will come to you to be engaged in the service of the preaching mission. Simply go forward to preach the message of love of God as given by Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, giving it your total effort. No worldly force will be able to disrupt this effort. We are with you always.
“In every town and village of the earth, the chanting of My name will be propagated.”
There is no other remedy other than nam-sankirtan in this Kaliyug. It is true for all places, not only for India. You propagate this message throughout the world. Why should anybody be deprived?”
Then after He came to Kolkata at Ultadanga Road, and from there he propagated the teachings of Mahaprabhu throughout the world.

articles.title: Labdhva Sudurlabham Idam…
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: At 1, Ultadanga Road Srila Bhakti Siddhant Saraswati Goswami Thakur used to deliver sermons on Srimad Bhagavatam which is the quintessence of all Scriptures. Many people used to come to listen him. There, he spoke on this particular verse from 11th Canto for one full month. Even after commenting on this verse for one month, he was not satisfied and wanted to speak more about it! Listening to his powerful teachings regarding the rarest opportunity of the human birth and its actual purpose, two students of Scottish Church College, Kolkata, who were going back home after attending their college, could never go back home. They stayed in the Math for rest of their life. Such was the powerful preaching activities done by Srila Prabhupad. We cannot even imagine what he did.

blocks.text: I have heard from my most revered Gurudeva several times speak about his Gurudeva, our Param Gurudeva, grand Gurudeva, most venerable Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami Thakur. We had no opportunity to see Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami Thakur, we have seen only our Gurudeva. And Gurudeva in his delivering of sermons many times in different places reminded about him. Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur first started Gaudiya Math in Kolkata at Ultadanga Road. Then afterwards they shifted it to Bagh-bazar now. First math was started at Ultadanga Road. There our Param Gurudeva Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami Thakur was delivering sermons and many people were hearing. Anybody can come and hear. What happened there? He explained one verse from Srimad Bhagavatam, quintessence of all Scriptures. From the 11th canto, he explained that verse for one month. Still he was not satisfied, Can you imagine?

What is that verse? It is very important. ‘labdhva sudurlabham idam bahu-sambhavante manusyam arthadam anityam apiha dhirah turnam yateta na pated anu mrtyu yavan nihsheyasaya visayah khalu sarvath syat’. He explained this verse for 30 days yet he was not satisfied. I can say the meaning of that verse in five minutes. But that verse is identical with Krishna, Bhagavatam is identical with Krishna, one with Krishna and transcendental, it is transcendental sound. He (Krishna) is Infinite, Absolute, Complete Reality. Bhagavatam is also complete Reality. Nobody can finish. For the eternal benefit of the conditioned souls, of the neophytes or aspirants of pure devotion, what our Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu made pastimes at Puri? He heard Bhagavatam 7th canto Prahlad Charitra and 4th Canto Druva Charitra not once, hundred times from Gadadhar Pandit Goswami. After that again Chaitanya Mahaprabhu says I want to hear. I have not heard the full topic from beginning to the end (but I say) Oh I have already heard, I want to hear something new. Bhagavatam is identical with Krishna, nobody can finish by tasting its sweetness. If anybody says like that, it is wrong thing.

Brahma in his prayer to Sri Krishna in 10th Canto, said ‘jananta eva janantu kim bahuktya na me prabho manaso vapuso vaco vaibhavam tava go-carah’. What is the meaning of this verse? Brahma, when he was infatuated he could not understand Krishna, he made the pastimes of not understanding. But that was not mentioned by Vedavyasa Muni in the Bhagavatam. Vedavyasa Muni never said a word that Brahma was playing the pastimes. Because conditioned souls of this world have got vanity, they will misunderstand. Even the creator of all universes, creator of all living beings, brahma could not understand then you think about your position. if you have submitted to him then you could understand. In his prayer, what Brahma is saying, if anybody is saying he has comprehended, he has realized Sri Krishna completely that be so. I do not want to say much words, I do not want to speak grandiloquently, of bombastically. Let them say. They, the wiseacre may think we are wise persons. Let them say that they can understand.

First thing is this. There is no equal to Him and more than Him. If a human being, conditioned soul can know Him by his own caliber, by his own intellectual power, mental power, then God will lose His absolute position. Without His grace nobody can know. Grace always flows down. Water always flows down, not upwards. If there is any vanity that region is completely sealed. Nobody can enter, that transcendental realm is completely sealed. But if you take absolute shelter, He is so merciful. If you are sincere immediately you will get. He is so merciful. But we have got no belief. We want to know Him by challenging mood. Then His maya will envelop us. You will not be able to understand. As per degree of submission you can understand. There are degrees of submission ad infinitum.

In higher mathematics you will find, infinite plus something is infinite, infinite minus something is infinite, infinite minus infinite is also infinite. Nobody can know Him or can finish their realization of Supreme Lord. If anybody says (so), he has got no knowledge of Supreme Lord. Ad infinitum, it will go on for infinite times. Every time you will find new fresh sweetness, every time ‘pratipadam purnamrta swadanam’. How you will see? If they say they know, let them know. I do not want to say much words, ‘jananta eva janantu kim bahuktya na me prabho manaso vapuso vaco vaibhavam tava go-carah’. Even I could not understand His own personal associates, cowherd boys, what to speak of Krishna. I could not understand them, I lifted them. I could not understand His transcendental realm, what to speak of Supreme Lord Sri Krishna.

Therefore, here what Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami Thakur (says) in this verse is very important. Nowadays you have to remember this and he spoke about this for one month and wanted to speak about it for another month, only one verse ‘labdhva sudarlabham idam bahu sambavante’. After numerous births, 8 million births you can get this human birth, after that 8 millions of aquatic animals, then trees, plants etc immobile living beings. Jagadish Bose, Scientist of India, Bengal, has proved that plants and trees have got life. It has already been written in the Vedas that the trees and plants they have got life, even mountains have got life. Immovable living beings 2 million and 9 hundred thousand aquatic animals, 2 million trees, plants, mountains etc immovable, immobile living beings. And worms 1 million, birds 1 million and beasts 3 million. After that 8 million births, after so much suffering, we have got this human birth. Let us think about it, 4 hundred thousand births, here it is mentioned we have got this human birth, but there is no guarantee that you will get this human birth again. No guarantee.

You have heard the name Bharath, the eldest son of Rishab Deva. He renounced his family and the kingdom in his young age and went to forest to perform penance. There he had a connection with one young-one of a deer. I do not want to say the history. At the time of death, he was thinking of that deer. ‘yam yam vapi smaran bhaavam tyajaty ante kalevaram tam tam evai ti Kauteya sadaa tad bhaava bhaavi tah’. At the time of death whatever you will think, you will have accordingly a birth. Such a person, who remembers that I came to the forest to worship Supreme Lord. By seeing one young-one of a deer I had some affection and gave some energy to him. At the time of death, I was thinking about him, that there are so many ferocious animals, who will protect him? While thinking like this I died, I was born as deer. Whatever we shall think at the time of death according to that you will get the birth, in Gita it is said clearly. Then, there is no certainty, although it is written four hundred thousand births, we say four lakhs human birth, but there may be slip.

This is one evidence from the scripture. And I have got practical evidence, in Assam, near Goalpara math. I do not want to say it, practical. He became a dog. There is no certainty. ‘Labdhva sudurlabham idam bahu sambhavante’. After numerous births, so many distresses and in the mother’s womb so many pains, suffering is extreme but those who have got their lively-hood by eating fish and flesh, they have killed all the fishes and beasts, they have killed so they have to suffer, tremendous suffering. We have passed through so many births like warm and birds etc and then we have got this human birth. ‘Sudurlabham’, after so much suffering, so much difficulty we have got this birth but it is non-eternal, transient, mortal. Any moment we may lose this chance. Nowadays nobody is said to be safe. In today’s situation of world nobody can say if he goes out he can come (back) alive. Nobody can say. Gradually it is deteriorating. Why we should make late? Just from this moment (start bhajana). When our Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami Thakur was explaining this. one day, as I heard from our Gurudeva, two students of Scottish Arts College of Kolkata, they are coming from the college and going towards their destination. On the way they have heard that some great saint is there. Let us see. For seeing, with books they entered and saw Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami Thakur, a dazzling personality, and golden complexion. They never saw such person. They were very much attracted (and thinking). He was explaining this ‘turnam yateta’. Don’t make late, immediately, just this moment(start haribhajan). Don’t spoil your time, a moment’s time without serving Krishna. You avoid unnecessary words, unnecessary things, do not do it. You have to repent if you do it. Any moment you may lose this human birth and again you shall get this human birth there is no certainty. ‘Turnam yateta’, so immediately you should start, he said this looking at the new two students. They sat at the end. They were afraid, what is this, this Swamiji was looking at us, why? He did not allow us to go from this place. They asked,”Swamiji, what you wanted to say? You do not allow us to go to our house? Oh No! We have committed a great mistake, (they thought) inside. Now they thought, how we can get ourselves freed from this place. We have to go back to our house.
They thought, Let us say this reason. “Swamiji, if my house catches fire, am I not to go there to extinguish it?”
“If your house will burn, what you have to do, nothing.”
“What sort of Sadhu! Even if My house gets burnt, you think it’s to be nothing?“
“Yes, nothing.”
“If I could not extinguish that fire then other houses will burn.”

“Let the whole world get burn, what do you lose? You have come from the world? brahma-bhutah prasannatma, na socati na kanksati samah sarvesu bhutesu mad-bhaktim labhate param’, in Gita it is said. Brahma-bhutah, you are chetana. As long as that consciousness exists in your body so long you have got personality, thinking, feeling and willing. When it leaves the body, a dead body is not considered a person. It may be retained chemically for a long time. Nobody will consider the dead body as a person. Person is the consciousness. Consciousness has come from Consciousness. Nothing cannot be the cause of something. The highest Supreme Reality is All Conscience, All Knowledge, All Bliss, All Existence, He is Purna Saccidananda. You are coming from Him.” Taittiriya Upanisad says ‘yato va imani bhutani jayante yena jatani jivanti yat prayantyabhisamvisanti tad vijijnasasva tad brahma’. It is not Gaudiya math’s writing. All the jivas are coming from Para-brahma, Supreme Lord; coming not from impersonal form of Brahma, from ‘apadan karan’ that is ablative case. So, there is a form, transcendental spiritual form. He is not formless. All the jivas are coming and Brahma is maintaining them, sustaining them. This is instrumental cause, parama karan and where it will go, it will go to Supreme Lord. When there are 3 cases ablative case, instrumental case and vocative case (saptam vibhakti) how it can be impersonal? Supreme Lord is the Person Infinite, whole universe is coming out of Him. They are by Him, they are in Him. These 3 cases prove that Supreme Lord has got form. He has got qualities, transcendental spiritual qualities.

So here it is said, turnam yateta na pated anyu-mrtyu yavan nihsreyasaya visayah khalu sarvatah syat. Eternal Reality is Supreme Lord and we are eternally connected with Him. We have come from Him, in Him, by Him, we should remain for Him. This world has got no connection with you, with your soul. The whole world is burnt, what you will lose? You are from Krishna, you are in Krishna, you are by Krishna. You should start bhajan from this moment. If you go on the road, you may die.“

At that time when Saraswati Goswami Thakur was there, it was not so much rampant. Even that time he was saying it. But nowadays they are killing everybody without consideration whether there is enmity or not, to serve their purpose. Boys, children, and women without are being killed without any consideration whether enemies or not, destroying them. So nowadays by seeing this directly we should not sleep, we should not spoil our time. We should immediately start.
“Don’t go, on the road you may die.”
Then they could not go. They are attracted by his supernatural spiritual personality. They remained here, they did not go back.

articles.title: Announcement of Prabhupad’s Departure in Gaudiya Magazine
articles.author: Sree Chaitanya Gaudiya Math
articles.excerpt: At about 5:30 A.M., on Thursday, January 1, 1937, on Krishna caturthī, Srila Prabhupada entered the eternal abode, joining Sri Radha-Govinda in the predawn pastimes (niśānta-līlā). At the end of every night, Sri Radha-Krishna lie intertwined in an embrace, becoming as one body. It is at this moment, when Their united form of Sri Gaurasundara is eternally manifest, that Varshabhanavi-dayita Dasa, Their servant, joined them. This is the announcement of his departure as published in Gaudiya Magazine.

blocks.text: Last Narayan 4, 450 of the Chaitanya era, at the end of the Thursday night, Paush 16, 1343 of the Bengali calendar, on Friday morning, January 1, 1937, Paramahaṁsa Parivrājakācārya Om VishnuViṣṇupada Śrīla Śrīmadla Bhakti Siddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupada, joined his eternal service in the predawn pastimes (niśānta-līlā), the first hour of the day’s eternal activities pastimes, of Sri Radha-Govinda. in the first hour of their eternal twenty-four cycle of activities. This is the same hour that his own gurudev, Om VishnuViṣṇupada Śrī Śrīla Gaura Kishor Das BabajiPrabhu entered into nitya-līlā. Prabhupada was the great acharya of the Gaudiya Vaiṣṇava sampradaya and its only protector, the ninth in descent from Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, and the best of the followers of Sri Svarupa Damodar and Śrī Rupa Gosvāmī.

The meaning of entering the lila into eternal pastimes (nitya-līlā) at this hour is understood clearly by those who are intimate with him for it is directly experienced in their hearts, but a hint, based on the words of realized souls, is being can be given here. At the end of the night, Sri Radha-Govind are locked in a divine unbreakable embrace, gāḍhāliṅgana-nirbhedam āptau. Jayadeva Gosvāmī has indicated this situation with the word naktam in the first verse of Gīta-govindam which begins meghair meduram ambaram. When Sri Radha-Govind are joined together like this, they take on their combined form of Sri Gaurasundar. It is this auspicious moment that Sri Vārṣabhānavī Dayita Das Prabhu chose to make his entry into their pastimes.

Śrīla Prabhupada is like the sun of the Gaudiya sampradaya, as he is identical with its acharyas Sri Rupa and Sri Svarupa Damodar. But now that this sun of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu’s sampradaya has set, darkness has descended not only on the preachers in the sky of the Gaudiya sampraday Math lineage, but on the entire world. It seems that the direct light of guileless unadulterated devotion will once again be hidden from the view of the world’s people. Our only hope is that this luminary amongst spiritual teachers sufficiently inspired his sincere followers with such an unparalleled desire to serve the feet of the Lord Adhokshaja, with such ever-fresh enthusiasm, and instilled in them such paramount and rare ideals of practice and preaching, that the stream which passed through Sri Svarupa and Sri Rupa and then through Bhaktivinode Ṭhākura will only continue to gather more force and flow into the world. In our hearts, we consider nothing else to be possible even in our worst imaginings. From the blessings that he gave just before passing on entering into his eternal service, we know that by adhering faithfully to his teachings and propagating them, we will be able to get his direct, personal association and will be able to find all the strength we need. Furthermore, by preaching fearlessly, with an independent spirit without any expectation, and with the force of character that comes of sincere service and fidelity, we will be able to practice and preach the gospel of Sri Gaurasundar, our master’s master, throughout the world. By so doing, we are assured that his blessings will continue to rain down on us even more profusely. This faith is the sole lamppost illuminating the path of pure devotion, which is strewn with countless obstacles.

We, the Gaudiya’s writers, are today without any shelter, as we will no longer be able to show our articles to him who was the preserver of Swarupa Damodar and Rupa Goswami’s devotional doctrines and Raghunath‘s tradition. Śrīla Prabhupada would eagerly read every article which was to be published in the Gaudiya. He would give us blessings and show the deepest satisfaction with our efforts. Now, even though he we will no longer be able to do experience this directly, we will not be entirely devoid of his blessings nor of the spiritual strength arising from his mercy. We are not without succor, for he left us the gift of service to those who know the doctrines of pure devotion as taught by Bhaktivinode Ṭhākura, and hence we are not deprived of his eternal blessings and mercy through this service we shall gain the capacity to understand his most confidential desires and doctrines.

articles.title: Contemplating Separation from Srila Prabhupad
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Kamal Madhusudan Maharaj
articles.excerpt: Although when the sun has set, it may be outside the vision of the living beings in any given country, it cannot be concluded that the sun has become extinct. Similarly, when the associates of Bhagavan perform their disappearance pastimes, they may remain in a domain beyond our range of vision, yet they are eternally His companions, nourishing Bhagavan Sri Gauranga’s and Bhagavan Sri Krishna’s pastimes.

blocks.text: External Celebration, Internal Separation

Nineteen years ago, oṁ viṣṇupāda paramahaṁsa Śrī Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda – who is the embodiment of the compassion potency (karuṇa-śakti) of the deity of vipralambha-rasa, Śrī Gaurasundara, and who is the sole, true friend of the jīvas – enacted his disappearance pastime. On the 16th day of the last month, Pauṣa, members of the community of Sārasvata-Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas venerated and duly honoured Śrīla Prabhupāda’s disappearance day in accordance with the proper conventions, as per their respective qualification (adhikāra). Every year, all of us who have taken shelter of Śrīla Prabhupāda have been worshipping this most sacred tithi, the best of all holy days, according to appropriate standards. But in the true sense, in how many of us, has the pain of separation from Śrīla Prabhupāda been able to make even the slightest mark in our hearts? This is known only to Śrīla Prabhupāda himself. From the perspective of making external arrangements for a celebration, I am flawless, unfailing and undeviating, but as far as my internal condition is concerned, who will ascertain that? For an individual like me, who am cheated by external vision, bereft of sambandhagyāna, or true knowledge of my relationship with the Lord, stricken with extreme greed for wealth, women and fame, and infatuated by empty pomp, where is there a question of feeling separation from my Prabhu, my dear-most master?

Without sambandha-gyāna, there is no question of actually feeling separation. Yet in defiance of my overwhelming lack of qualification, there comes, from a certain direction, an extraordinarily mighty hope: the unprecedented compassion of patita-pāvana Śrīla Prabhupāda for the fallen souls. Thus far, compassion of this amplitude in the deed of delivering lost and fallen jīvas has not been displayed by any among the most intimate associates of Śrī Gaura. Some, having earned Śrīla Prabhupāda’s true mercy, have become blessed. Within the inner recesses of their hearts, they are feeling continuous, unending separation from him. Consequently, they are experiencing success, deriving considerable inspiration in the realm of bhajana.
Spiritual Anguish – A Source of Boundless Joy

Even in the material world, when a worldly relationship is dissolved due to unavoidable death, a person who was deeply enamored by another, may be gripped in an intense grief that seems intolerable. In certain cases, the pain of material separation assumes such an extreme degree that, unable to endure it, some people neglect their own body, their highest object of attachment, to such an extent that they bring about their own self-annihilation, their death. If a person can react so intensely to the severance of a temporary, insignificant relationship within this mortal coil – a relationship wholly in the realm of mundane lust – then how acute and unbearable is separation from that supremely excellent eternal entity belonging to the transcendental realm of Vaikuṇṭha? Such intensity defies words. The grief resulting from the severance of mundane relationships, which are based on ignorance and born of delusion, is full of despondency and yields nothing but anguish. Conversely, transcendental separation results in a simultaneous blend of absorption in unfathomable bliss and heart-wrenching sobs of lamentation in absence from the dear one. Even though such cries are an expression of extreme sorrow, it is not distressing like mundane grief. In the realm of non-existence, where everything is temporary, all things are a source of trouble. But on the platform of viśuddhasattva in the realm of true and complete existence, a sense of lacking, or absence, occurs – yet it is comprised of supreme astonishment and enhances the moods of vipralambha-rasa. The intimate associates of Śrīla Prabhupāda, who experience intense pain in separation from him, constantly feel his absence, and, inspired by that, they engage in fulfilling his heart’s innermost desires (mano’bhīṣṭa). Wherever the experience of separation yields slothfulness and consequently generates laxity in service, it is to be under - stood that it arises from the modes of passion and ignorance. But if the intensity of transcendental separation produces inertia, it is not troublesome like mundane inertia, but full of the experience of the most bountiful happiness.
Transcendental Separation Stimulates the Mood of Service

For those whose perception is based on ‘eyes of flesh’, the moment any obstacle to their enjoyment arises, they become seized by a despondency and idleness born of ignorance. But for those whose vision is founded in the Vedas or the holy name, the grief of transcendental separation profusely increases their enthusiasm to serve. Those who are servants of śrī guru are neither the champions of pious fruitive action (karma) nor of empiric knowledge (jṣāna). As the carriers of śrī gurupāda-padma’s shoes, their vow is to remain exclusively engaged in fulfilling the innermost desires of his heart, everywhere and always. karmāvalambakāḥ kecit kecij-jṣāna-avalambakāḥ vayantu haridāsānāṁ pāda-trāṇa-avalambakāḥ Padyāvalī (58) This means, “Some, having adopted the path of fruitive action, are karmīs, while others, having taken shelter of empiric knowledge, have become jṣānīs, but we, the servants of the servants of Śrī Hari, are the carriers of His servant’s shoes.” In separation from śrī guru, some of his servants have wholly surrendered their very selves to him, having accrued within their hearts the multitude of teachings that issued from his lotus mouth. And in carrying out those instructions to the letter, they obtain millions of times more stimulus to serve than when he was manifest.

There are others whose aim and object is not to fulfil the innermost desires of gurudeva’s heart; yet externally they appear extremely enthusiastic to serve. We must understand, however, that the driving force behind their endeavours is like that of the champions of karma – extraneous (anyābhilāṣa) and laced with a greed for worldly reputation.
Internal Motive is Beyond External Judgement

According to varying qualifications (adhikāra) and consequent gradations in motive, one deed may be classified as either forbidden action (vikarma), prescribed action (karma), knowledge (jṣāna), or devotion to the Supreme Lord (bhakti). If one performs hari-kīrtana to obtain sense gratification that is scripturally unauthorized, but which may be either lawful or unlawful from a materialistic perspective, then that kīrtana is to be known as vikarma. If one’s motive is to attain scripturally authorized happiness, either in this world or the next, then that hari-kīrtana will be classified as karma. If one’s motive in performing hari-kīrtana is to achieve liberation, then that kīrtana will be known as jṣāna. And if one performs hari-kīrtana driven by a desire to render cent-percent loving service to śrī guru and the Vaiṣṇavas in all respects, then that hari-kīrtana is bhakti. Individuals of astute intelligence never judge any action on the basis of external performance. Rather, the sole object of their deliberation is the intention behind an action. Even if, from an external standpoint, Hiraṇyakaśipu’s observance of austerity and Rāvaṇa’s acceptance of the dress of a renunciant (tridaṇḍi) are considered praiseworthy, the intentions behind their actions are undoubtedly condemnable.
The Vaiṣṇava Never Leaves Us

Śrī guru and the Vaiṣṇavas are not entities subject to birth and death like those beings bound by the laws of fruitive action. Like Śrī Bhagavān, they exhibit the pastimes of appearance (prakaṭa) and disappearance (aprakaṭa) in this world. na karmabandhanaṁ janma vaiṣṇavānāṣca vidyate viṣṇoranucaratvaṁ hi mokṣamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ Padma-Purāṇa (quoted in Hari-bhakti-vilāsa 10.113) The meaning is “The Vaiṣṇavas have no material birth, nor are they bound by the laws of karma. The learned declare that attaining the position of Lord Viṣṇu’s associate servant is indeed mokṣa.” Although when the sun has set, it may be outside the vision of the living beings in any given country, it cannot be concluded that the sun has become extinct. Similarly, when the associates of Bhagavān perform their disappearance pastimes, they may remain in a domain beyond our range of vision, yet they are eternally His companions, nourishing Bhagavān Śrī Gaurāṅga’s and Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. Even if we cannot directly receive Śrīla Prabhupāda’s instructions (upadeśa) and directives (nirdeśa), the fact remains that from a location concealed from our eyes he is protecting and nourishing us in all respects.
Śrīla Prabhupāda Brought the Flood of Harikīrtana

He left a wealth of teachings healthful to the consciousness of the living beings. Each word is consciousness awakening. The teachings of Śrīla Prabhupāda – who is non-different from Śrī Baladeva – transmit spiritual strength (cidbala) into us, and are our sole support and shelter. In his pastime of preaching the cherished aims of Śrī Caitanya’s heart (mano’bhīṣṭa), within a very short period of time he released, through multifarious channels, the unimpaired stream of Śrī Caitanya’s teachings. How wonderful are the sublime ideals he established in this world, proving himself to be the best of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī’s followers in the line of Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, and the bestower of compassion upon all living entities! His accomplishments cannot be enumerated. His work to benefit the world has earned the unreserved commendation of all honest and genuine people, irrespective of their nation or caste. Innumerable learned and noble persons placed themselves at his feet and, upon hearing the hari-kathā that emanated from his lotus mouth, discovered their eternal welfare. By bringing a great deluge of hari-kīrtana to this world – which was deprived of it and duly stricken, he established an ideal utterly beyond compare. Furthermore, the originality he exhibited in his pastimes as ācārya, while preserving the specialty of the stream of teachings coming in the line of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, is unprecedented.
Transcendental Separation – Beyond Expression

How heart-rending is separation from one’s dear-most guru, the Vaiṣṇavas and other godly personalities! It finds no means of expression in any language of the world, a world saturated with anxieties and limitations. Language can only serve to allude to the direction of the heart’s transcendental, loving emotions. Even so, those who are fully conversant with the absolute truths regarding the Lord and His exalted pure devotees – which are accessible through realization – can comprehend the depth and importance of transcendental loving sentiments, even if they are only expressed to a slight degree through language. Upon the disappearance of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī Prabhu, his foremost follower Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī Prabhu manifested the painful emotions of his heart as follows: śūnyāyate mahā-goṣṭhaṁ girīndro ’ jagarāyate vyāghra-tuṇḍāyate kuṇḍaṁ jīvātu-rahitasya me Śrī Prārthanāśraya-caturdaśaka (11) This means, “In separation from Śrī Rūpa, who was the sole sustainer of my life, this Vraja-maṇḍala appears as if vacant, Girirāja-Govardhana appears like a python, and Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa like the mouth of a tiger.” In Śrīla Dāsa Gosvāmī’s transcendental mood of separation from Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī Prabhu – who is the all in all of his very life (prāṇa) – his cherished places of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, his more cherished Girirāja Govardhana, and even his most cherished Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa, all appeared lifeless. It seemed that everything was lost and plunged into darkness. The intense state of mind attained by mahā-bhāgavata Vaiṣṇavas in their divine separation is touched upon in the language of Śrīla Narottama Ṭhākura:

pāṣāṇe kuṭibo māthā anale paśibo - I will dash my head upon a stone or enter into fire. Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta (Madhya-līlā 8.247) also gives evidence of this. Śrīman Mahāprabhu inquired, “duḥkha madhye kon duḥkha haya gurutara – among all sorrows, what sorrow is the topmost?” In response, Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya said, “kṛṣṇa-bhakta viraha vinā duḥkha nāhi dekhi para – I know of no greater sorrow than separation from the pure devotee of Kṛṣṇa.”
Śrīla Prabhupāda’s Uncompromising Compassion

Only one who is a Vaiṣṇava can realize separation from another Vaiṣṇava. Transcendental separation cannot be realized by those on the platforms of enjoyment and renunciation. Śrīla Prabhupāda, who is an intimate associate of Śrī Gaura, appeared on this Earth by Śrī Gaura’s will solely for the purpose of fulfilling the innermost desire of Gaura’s heart. Śrīla Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, a śaktyāveśa-puruṣa, meaning ‘a person suffused with the great potency of the Lord,’ appeared as the instrument of Śrī Gaurasundara’s prediction: prithivite ache jata nagarādi-grāma sarvatra pracāra haibe mora nāma Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata (Antya-khaṇḍa 4.126) In every town and village of the earth, the chanting of My name will be propagated. Thus he has distributed the eternal benediction of this prophesy by drenching the world in a deluge of topics about Śrī Hari. Those individuals who are sāragrāhī, seekers of the essence, pursue the welfare of their souls, and it is for certain that a day will come when they will realize the essential nature and inner significance of Śrīla Prabhupāda’s fulfilling this prophesy. In his worldwide preaching, Śrīla Prabhupāda’s intention was not to gain material fame by astonishing the people of the world with oral recitations of scripture that show indifference to the real meaning of the Upaniṣads and vedānta-sūtra, like one carrying hackneyed load, for to do so would be to immolate the self on the sacrificial stake of subservience to the opinions of the masses, who are averse to Bhagavān. Pained at heart upon seeing the wretched state of human-kind, which was stricken with grief from suffering the threefold material miseries, Śrīla Prabhupāda performed preaching activities that pervaded the entire world. His intention was to install the kingdom of Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the heart of every living entity through hari-kīrtana. He did not expend one drop of blood to increase party majority by appointing lifeless, paid preachers: vrajavāsīgaṇa, pracāraka-dhana pratiṣṭhā-bhikṣuka tā’rā nahe ’śava prāṇa āche tā’ra, se hetu pracāra, pratiṣṭhāśā-hīna-kṛṣṇa-gāthā saba Vaiṣṇava ke? (18) Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda The residents of Vraja are the only true preachers in this world, as they are endowed with the wealth of kṛṣṇa-prema. They are not devoid of life, and therefore they do not hanker after worldly distinction. They are full of the vitality that comes from loving Kṛṣṇa, and they go out and speak about Him. Whatever they say is free from the desire for prestige. In these words alone, he has manifested the true criteria for preaching the topics of Śrī Hari. “Satyaṁ paraṁ dhīmahi – I meditate upon the Absolute Truth.” As the proponent of genuine truth, he waved the victory flag of ŚrīmadBhāgavatam’s message, thereby subduing the deception of illusion. In this way, Śrīla Prabhupāda’s reputation as a Vaiṣṇava (vaiṣṇavī-pratiṣṭhā) has been celebrated everywhere. An effort to unscrupulously commingle genuine Truth with untruth, or customary truth, and thus become attendant to the disposition of those averse to the Truth, was never once observed in his character. In the unconscious world, vox populi, or vox dei (meaning ‘the opinion of the general masses is equal to the opinion of God’) prevails. By propagating the kīrtana of Śrī Caitanya’s teachings, Śrīla Sarasvatī Ṭhākura opposed this current of thought of the unconscious world and endeavoured up to his last breath to establish us in our inherent consciousness. Genuine truth cannot be ascertained by public opinion. This was Śrīla Prabhupāda’s basic premise. As a result of his lifelong struggle to oppose the innumerable followers of incidental truth, those in whose ears the message containing the real Truth has entered have attained the success of their human form. Those who took shelter of him, in recompense for their very selves being fully sold at his lotus feet, were infused with his mercy potency. They have preached and are continuing to do so. Like porters, they carry everywhere the message of Śrī Caitanya that emanated from his mouth. For them, there is no question of desiring worldly reward. A Humble Petition To fulfil the desires of Śrī Gurupāda-padma, who has fulfilled Śrī Caitanya’s innermost desires, indeed constitutes true service to guru. And it is through such service that divine separation is realized. Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-dayita dāsa Prabhu, of his own volition, sprinkled the stream of his mercy upon everyone, everywhere, without considering who is superior or who is inferior. I nurture within my heart the hope of becoming the dust of the lotus feet of that supremely merciful Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-dayita dāsa Prabhu, life after life. śrī caitanya-mano ’bhīṣṭaṁ sthāpitaṁ yena bhū-tale svayaṁ rūpaḥ kadā mahyaṁ dadāti sva-padāntikam Śrī Prema-bhakti-candrikā (1.38) When will Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī give me the shelter of his lotus feet? Because he understood the innermost desire of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he was able to establish His mission in this world and is very dear to the Lord.
